conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. I'll be your doctor during your stay. You're here to start hemodialysis, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s right. I’ve been feeling more tired and short of breath lately, especially when I walk.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You mentioned swelling in your legs and itching too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, my legs are swollen up to my knees, and the itching is all over. It’s been bothering me at night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. With your kidney function being very low, fluid and waste build up, which can cause those symptoms.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve also been gaining weight, though I’m not sure how much. And I can’t lie flat because of my belly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your polycystic kidneys are quite large, about the size of watermelons, which explains the abdominal pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s hard to find clothes that fit. But I’m glad we’re starting dialysis now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll start your first session today. You have a fistula in your right arm, which is good—it means we can use it for dialysis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it was placed a few months ago. Is it ready to use?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s mature and functioning well. We’ll begin hemodialysis shortly. You should feel better after a few sessions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How are you feeling after your first dialysis session?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel a bit tired, but my breathing seems a little easier already.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a good sign. We removed about two liters of fluid today, which should help with your swelling and breathing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that’s a lot! No wonder I feel lighter.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’ll do two more sessions before you go home. Your blood pressure is already improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been on a lot of medications. Will those change?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, because your kidneys aren’t filtering drugs like before, some meds need to be stopped or adjusted.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Which ones are we stopping?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re stopping atenolol, valsartan, furosemide, iron, darbepoetin, and hectorol. Your dialysis center will manage anemia and bone health now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And what about my blood pressure? I’m still on amlodipine and lisinopril?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, those are safer to continue. We stopped atenolol because your heart rate was low—likely from the drug building up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been on atenolol for my atrial fibrillation. Is that still under control?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your EKG showed sinus bradycardia, not afib. We’ll keep amiodarone and coumadin. Your INR is stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. And coumadin—I need to keep that monitored, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Your dialysis center will manage your coumadin now. If not, contact your cardiologist.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. We did a chest X-ray yesterday to make sure your heart and lungs are ready for dialysis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And? Is everything okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Your heart is at the upper limit of normal size, but no fluid in the lungs. That’s good news.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. How’s my second dialysis session going to be different?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Similar to the first. We’ll remove more fluid and clean your blood. You’re tolerating it well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve now had two sessions. How are you feeling overall?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My legs are less swollen, and I’m sleeping better. The itching is still there, though.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The itching may take a few more sessions to improve. We’ve started nephrocaps for your vitamins.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the PPD test you placed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a TB screening. You’ll need to have it read at your primary doctor’s office in a couple days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve completed three dialysis sessions and are doing well. We’re planning to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What do I need to do when I get home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take your new medications as listed. Most are now at bedtime. Your next dialysis is scheduled for Monday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if I feel confused or nauseated?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call your doctor right away. Those could be signs your levels are off. Otherwise, keep your follow-ups.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. You did well. We’ll see you at your next appointment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a final check before discharge. Any new symptoms?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I feel stable. A bit weak, but better than when I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s expected. Your body is adjusting. Keep up with your diet and fluid limits.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll make sure to do that. And I’ll get the PPD test read.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. You’re cleared to go home. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll be in touch with your dialysis team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—we discussed DNR/DNI. You’re comfortable with that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I don’t want aggressive resuscitation. I want comfort care if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s documented in your chart. Thank you for discussing that with us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate your respect for my wishes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Of course. That’s part of good care. Let’s get your discharge papers ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready when you are.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll have a nurse go over your meds and instructions one more time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I want to make sure I get it right.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Absolutely. We’re here to support you every step of the way.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel much more confident now.
